record.paper_title: SYMMETRY AND COLORINGS: SOME RESULTS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
record.original_question: How quickly do the sequences {ms([n], r)}_{n=1}^{∞} and {bms([n], r)}_{n=1}^{∞} converge to their common limit ms([0, 1], r)?

evidence.quote: (1) ms([0, 1], r) = lim n→∞ ms([n], r) = inf n∈ N ms([n], r) for any r ∈ N;
(2) bms([0, 1], r) = lim n→∞ bms([n], r) = inf n∈ N bms([n], r) for any r ∈ N;
8.5. Question. How quickly the sequences {ms([n], r)}∞ n=1 and {bms([n], r)}∞ n=1 converge to their limit ms([0, 1], r)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer n ≥ 1 let [n] = {1, 2, …, n}, equipped with the family of central symmetries s_c : x ↦ 2c − x (c ∈ ½ℤ). A subset B ⊆ [n] is called symmetric if s_c(B) = B for some c. A coloring of [n] is a map χ : [n] → {1, …, r}; a subset is monochromatic if χ is constant on it. Define

  MS([n], r) = min over all r-colorings χ of [n] of the maximum cardinality of a monochromatic symmetric subset of [n],
  ms([n], r) = MS([n], r) / n.

Analogously, a fractional r-coloring of [n] is a map χ : [n] → Δ_r, where Δ_r = {(p_1,…,p_r) ∈ ℝ_{≥0}^r : Σ p_i = 1}. The "monochromatic mass" in color i of a subset B is Σ_{x ∈ B} χ(x)_i. Define

  BMS([n], r) = inf over fractional r-colorings χ of the supremum, over symmetric subsets B ⊆ [n] and colors i, of Σ_{x ∈ B} χ(x)_i,
  bms([n], r) = BMS([n], r) / n.

For the unit interval [0, 1] equipped with central symmetries s_c(x) = 2c − x (c ∈ ℝ), and r-colorings χ : [0, 1] → {1, …, r} measurable in the appropriate sense, set

  ms([0, 1], r) = inf_χ sup{ λ(B) : B ⊆ [0,1] symmetric and monochromatic for χ },

where λ denotes Lebesgue measure. It is known that

  ms([0, 1], r) = lim_{n→∞} ms([n], r) = inf_{n ∈ ℕ} ms([n], r),
  ms([0, 1], r) = lim_{n→∞} bms([n], r) = inf_{n ∈ ℕ} bms([n], r),

for every r ∈ ℕ.

Problem. Determine the rate of convergence: for each fixed r ∈ ℕ, give sharp asymptotic bounds on ms([n], r) − ms([0, 1], r) and on bms([n], r) − ms([0, 1], r) as n → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in surveys on symmetry and colorings by Banakh, Verbitsky, Vorobets, and Protasov. Web searches did not reveal a published paper establishing sharp convergence rates for ms([n], r) and bms([n], r) toward ms([0, 1], r); related papers continue to investigate values and bounds for these invariants but do not appear to settle the rate of convergence. Status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces ms(Ω, r) and the fractional variant; studies values for [n] and [0,1].
status_evidence.claim: Defines the invariants and treats discrete-to-continuous limits, but does not give rates of convergence.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry and colorings: Some results and open problems (arXiv:0901.3356)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems related to colorings of objects with symmetries.
status_evidence.claim: The convergence-rate question is listed among the open problems in this survey.
